articles.title: Apuestas y pronósticos Levante vs Barcelona
articles.standfirst: Sportium te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Levante y al Barcelona en el Ciutat de València correspondiente a la quinta jornada de LaLiga
articles.summary: Sportium te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta al Levante y al Barcelona en el Ciutat de València correspondiente a la quinta jornada de LaLiga
articles.body: El Levante recibe al Barcelona este viernes en el Ciutat de València, en el partido correspondiente a la quinta jornada de LaLiga 26/27. El conjunto granota afronta el encuentro tras un inicio irregular pero con destellos de gran nivel. Empató 0-0 en su visita a La Rosaleda ante el Málaga, resultado que llegó después de golear por 5-2 al Betis en su feudo en la jornada anterior, un resultado que confirma que el equipo de Luis Castro puede hacer daño arriba pese a sus dudas defensivas. Favorito para el partido entre Levante y Barcelona Por su parte, el Barcelona llega a Valencia como único equipo con pleno de puntos en LaLiga, doce de doce posibles, y en un momento de forma arrollador que también ha trasladado a la Champions League tras su reciente victoria continental. El conjunto de Hansi Flick afronta este desplazamiento apenas unos días después de su compromiso europeo de mitad de semana, aunque su enorme profundidad de plantilla le permite rotar sin perder un ápice de nivel competitivo. Con todos estos datos, las casas de apuestas dan como amplio favorito al Barcelona. Sportium paga la victoria azulgrana a cuota 1.2, por 7 del empate y 11 de la victoria del cuadro granota. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una de las alternativas más interesantes del encuentro. El Levante ha demostrado capacidad ofensiva con los cinco goles anotados al Betis, aunque también dejó su portería a cero en su última salida ante el Málaga. El Barcelona, por su parte, no ha dejado de marcar en ninguno de sus cuatro partidos de liga, pero tampoco ha logrado mantener su portería intacta en todas sus salidas. Con estos datos, según las apuestas deportivas, la probabilidad de que ambos equipos anoten es alta. Sportium paga a 1.73 el "sí" y a 2 el "no". Número total de goles (Over/Under) El mercado de goles apunta hacia un partido con mucho fútbol ofensivo, apoyado sobre todo en el potencial del Barcelona, que ha marcado 17 goles en sus cuatro primeras jornadas. El Levante, aunque más irregular, también ha mostrado que puede firmar partidos con muchos goles, como el 5-2 ante el Betis. Con estos datos, Sportium sitúa la cuota del +2.5 totales a 1.3, por 3.25 del caso contrario. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de córners se presenta como una alternativa interesante para los apostantes. El Barcelona, con su juego de posesión y dominio territorial marcado por Flick, suele generar un volumen muy alto de saques de esquina en sus desplazamientos, algo que quedó patente en sus últimas salidas ligueras. El Levante, por su parte, ha mostrado en sus últimos partidos un perfil más replegado ante rivales de mayor entidad, lo que invita a pensar en una notable diferencia de córners a favor del conjunto catalán en este duelo. Sportium paga a 1.72 que se produzcan 9 o más córners, por 2 del caso contrario.

Esta liga oficial es la crème de la crème, con la recompensa inigualable de asistir a la Gala MARCA y ADN del Deporte para ser coronado con la exclusiva M roja. Os contamos toda la actualidad de las grandes ligas europeas en la cuenta de X (Twitter) @FantasyMARCA. Golazo decisivo de cabeza de Juan Iglesias, que sumó 13 puntos y es un chollo por 16,8 millones. Con 9 acabaron Castrín, Kike Salas y Suazo. Con 11 puntos Cabrera, que ya empieza a funcionar tras perderse el inicio de temporada por una sanción. Facundo Buonanotte, sorprendente MVP en San Mamés con 10 puntos en el Top MARCA (5 millones). Berenguer fue el mejor de los leones con 7 puntos. Dos goles y una asistencia de Mbappé para llegar a 20 puntos en el Top MARCA y borrar de un plumazo la decepción por el penalti fallado en Sevilla. Se destapó Carreras con un penalti provocado y un gol para irse a 15 puntos (cuesta 6,6 millones, capitán x3). Bellingham (13) y Güler (12), también brillaron. articles.title: 'CEO Neymar' reportedly pays £2m out of his own pocket to pay off Santos’ transfer ban, then signs his old Brazil buddies
articles.summary: Football News: Neymar's influence at Santos extends beyond the pitch as he reportedly pays £2m to lift a transfer ban, enabling the club to sign his former Brazil teammates including Coutinho and Arthur. Fans are excited about the recruitment efforts under Neymar's leadership.
articles.body: Neymar has continued to make his influence felt at Santos despite being sidelined with injury, with the Brazilian reportedly playing a decisive role in helping the club escape its transfer ban and bring in some familiar names.The Santos star has been out since suffering a thigh injury on September 2 during the second leg of the club's Brazilian Cup quarter-final against Palmeiras. While he has been unable to contribute on the pitch, his work away from it has helped Santos reshape their squad at a crucial stage of the season.The club had been prevented from registering new players after FIFA imposed a three-window transfer ban following a dispute with AS Monaco over the July 2023 transfer of Jean Lucas. Now, with the sanction lifted, Santos have moved quickly, bringing in former Liverpool players Arthur and Philippe Coutinho alongside other reinforcements.Neymar's marketing company reportedly paid €2m to lift Santos' banSantos' transfer ban dates back to July 1, 2025, when FIFA imposed the sanction after the Court of Arbitration for Sport rejected the club's appeal against AS Monaco's claim.Monaco had demanded €2 million over the transfer of Jean Lucas, leaving Santos unable to sign players during the three-window punishment.According to reports in L'Equipe, Neymar's family's sports marketing company, NR Sports, stepped in and allegedly paid the €2 million required to resolve the dispute and lift the ban.That intervention gave Santos the freedom to strengthen their squad, and the club wasted little time taking advantage of it.One of the first arrivals was Arthur Melo, the 30-year-old midfielder and Neymar’s former Brazil teammate, who joined on a short-term contract running until December 2026. The Brazilian defensive midfielder had struggled to establish himself in Europe after spells with Barcelona and Juventus, but his career also includes a brief and frustrating stint in the Premier League.Arthur joined Liverpool on loan from Juventus on September 1, 2022, with the Reds paying €4.5 million for the temporary deal. There had been hopes that he could eventually become an important player at Anfield after showing glimpses of his quality at Barcelona and Juventus.Instead, physical problems restricted him to just one appearance.Arthur made his Liverpool debut in a 4-1 Champions League defeat to Napoli, coming off the bench for 13 minutes. It was his only appearance for the club before he returned to Italy, with Liverpool ultimately choosing not to exercise their option to buy him.Santos have now offered him an opportunity to revive his career back in Brazil.Philippe Coutinho was persuaded by Neymar reunionCoutinho's Liverpool career could hardly have been more different.The 34-year-old spent five and a half seasons at Anfield after Brendan Rodgers signed him from Inter Milan for £8.5 million. He went on to make 201 appearances, scoring 54 goals, and became one of Liverpool's most influential attacking players.Coutinho was particularly important during Liverpool's Premier League title challenge in the 2013-14 season, forming part of an explosive attacking unit alongside Luis Suarez, Daniel Sturridge and Raheem Sterling.He subsequently became a key figure during the early years of Jurgen Klopp's reign before Barcelona paid £142 million to sign him in January 2018.That sale proved hugely significant for Liverpool, with the money helping the club finance major additions including Virgil van Dijk and Alisson as they built a squad capable of competing for the Premier League and Champions League.Coutinho's path has since taken him through Barcelona, Bayern Munich, Aston Villa and Vasco da Gama. His Vasco contract was terminated in February, and he was reportedly edging towards retirement before Santos emerged as an option.The prospect of playing alongside Neymar again proved decisive.The pair already share a long history, having played together for Brazil at the 2009 Under-17 World Cup and the 2022 World Cup. Coutinho has now agreed to join Santos, giving Neymar another familiar face to work with as the club attempt to climb the Brazilian football hierarchy.Everton Cebolinha has also joined the rebuilding project. The 30-year-old winger, who has won 25 international caps, had struggled to make an impact at Flamengo following his 2022 move from Benfica.His decision to move to Santos was heavily influenced by Neymar.“I was very close to signing in Russia, but the prospect of playing with Neymar was too tempting. I spoke to him and knew I had to go,” Everton said.Santos' ambitions are growing after Neymar's interventionThe arrivals come at a significant moment for Santos, who are attempting to turn their season around and compete on multiple fronts.They are chasing a place in the Copa Sudamericana semi-finals after beating Atletico Mineiro 2-0 in the first leg, while their league campaign has also prompted the club to strengthen now that the transfer ban has been lifted.Neymar's influence has therefore extended well beyond his role as Santos' star player. His reported involvement in resolving the €2m dispute has allowed the club to bring in players who would otherwise have been unavailable, while his personal relationships have helped convince experienced Brazilians to return to the club.The excitement among Santos supporters is already evident.UOL portal journalist Bruno Lima acknowledged that the new arrivals are not necessarily at the peaks of their careers, but argued that they can still make a difference to the team.“These new signings are still a long way from their peak level, but they will bring added value to the team,” Lima said.He added that supporters were not currently focused on the financial consequences because “the bill still has to be paid”, but that the signings had restored something Santos had been missing.“The fans have rediscovered their ambition. They are beside themselves with excitement and love this Neymar, who has developed into a CEO!”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Texas' stunning comeback win over Ohio State was everything college football should be — and it could soon be a thing of the past
articles.summary: Even in Week 2 of the season, every moment of Texas-Ohio State felt like a national championship was potentially on the line. But pro-expansion college footb...
articles.body:
AUSTIN, Texas — Hours before the out-of-nowhere comeback, before Darrell K. Royal-Texas Memorial Stadium pulsated with noise and shock, before the "SEC, SEC" chants spontaneously broke out over the din of elation and before thousands of forlorn Ohio State fans walked out into the night having that conversation about Ryan Day once again, a plume of burnt orange smoke seemed to linger over the field in the searing Texas heat.

It is a standard part of the pregame pyrotechnics here, but it was a particularly poignant image in the moments before a game like this one between two of college football's biggest brands and highest-ranked teams, with consequences that will take the rest of the season to figure out.

For 14 Saturdays of college football, we're all just waiting for the smoke to clear.

By the end of Texas 24, Ohio State 23 , it was a beautiful picture but an incomplete one, made possible only by a regular season that feels increasingly under attack by the powers that be. Year by year, the coaches and administrators at the mega-programs become less interested in playing games like these because the stakes are so high. And yet, without those high stakes of a limited playoff structure where losing this kind of game can knock you out, what kind of sport are you left with?

"Hopefully it pays dividends for us in December," Texas coach Steve Sarkisian said late Saturday night. "But we have a lot more meat on the bone we have to chew off here before we can start worrying about whether this win helps us get into a playoff or not."

Sarkisian is right, of course. We cannot know if one win in mid-September is a golden ticket to the postseason, even one over the No. 1 team in the country.

But imagine, if you will, this game being played in a world where the carrot at the end of all this is the 24-team College Football Playoff that power conference administrators seem to be sprinting toward as their preferred postseason format — perhaps as soon as next year.

Would it have seemed so dire and disappointing that Texas fell behind 23-3 in the third quarter? Would Sarkisian's series of fourth-down gambles to jumpstart his team — including a now-or-never roll of the dice on fourth-and-6 from his own 32-yard line with 11:45 left — have stirred the same crescendo of emotion throughout the 105,044 fans in attendance? Would we have learned as much about Arch Manning 's leadership and composure under real pressure as he completed 11 of his final 15 throws? Would anyone have even cared that Day went into turtle mode with the lead way too early and, frankly, blew a game Ohio State had no business losing?

"Beating a team like that is, in essence, a win for the season but also serves a little bit of a barometer of where we're at as a program," Sarkisian said. "They're not going anywhere and I told [Day], 'I hope we see you again because that would be a good sign for both of us.'"

And yet, the greatest thing that happened Saturday night — and the beauty of where college football is right now — is that we just don't know what it will all mean in December. If Day gets Ohio State to the playoff from here, overcoming a schedule that still includes Indiana, Oregon and USC, he will have earned his $12.5 million salary and then some. If he doesn't, the seat may warm up again.

Who knows? But at least every bit of it matters.

Realistically, in a 24-team playoff world, you can play this exact same game and it will not feel the same. Every player, every coach and every fan will know that two elite college football brands meeting on a stage like this will be a spectacle without a shred of consequence because they will both be ticketed for the postseason in the end.

Sure, everyone will want to win these games but they will not need to. Are we sure that's a good idea?

Because the essence of college football is what happened here Saturday night: Even in Week 2 of the season, every moment felt like a national championship was potentially on the line. Every dropped pass, every play call, every field goal attempt was massive, not just for this game, but how the rest of the season will play out.

Only college football has that intensity and those stakes every single week. That doesn't seem like something the sport should sacrifice for the sake of a little more TV money and a bloated playoff that gives everyone a trophy.

"We could be like some other teams and play Jones Junior High tonight and win 66-0, and I don't know what that does for us," Sarkisian said. "Tonight we found out that we can, and we've been close, and we've been knocking on the door and I do think it's helpful for us to play in a game like this, before conference play against an elite opponent, and come out on top. Surely that's helpful for us moving forward from a mentality standpoint."

It was funny to hear Sarkisian admit that because, in that very same room almost 10 months ago, he was singing a much different tune. At 9-3 after the regular season last year, Sarkisian knew that Texas probably wouldn't be in the CFP. So he cooked up a narrative that Texas should maybe consider canceling future non-conference games against real opponents because the Longhorns would have sailed into the postseason if they'd played a cupcake rather than taking the risk and losing to Ohio State, 14-7, in Week 1.

Now the shoe's on the other foot and Ohio State's margin for error is gone while Texas has banked a win that should give them a little breathing room if there are a couple slip-ups in SEC play.

In the end, there is no way to engineer the perfect schedule. Just like Sarkisian's fourth-down play calls, the entire sport is about taking calculated risks and accepting the consequences.

But the Texas turnabout is really a matter of college football facing an existential choice. It can either live with very good teams missing the playoff on occasion because some of them will lose games like this, or it will choose a 24-team playoff that makes games like this relatively meaningless.

We know, of course, what most college coaches and administrators are going to choose. They want the expanded playoff access, they want the TV money, they want the job security of making the playoff every year. They want the belief their lives will be less stressful if they just deconstruct the essence of sport they spent a century building and shift the pressure toward December and January rather than a hot night in September.

It's a big bet. And the cost might be significant.

Because everything about the scene in Austin on Saturday was perfect — including the fact that every player on the field and every fan in attendance left the stadium knowing they had just been part of something with real meaning that will shape the next 10 weeks of the season.

"We just had to get something going. I always knew we would be in it in the end," Manning said. "You dream of playing in games like this, hosting the No. 1 team in the country. How about that? Getting a win by one point? Let's go baby!"

Everyone lucky enough to witness it should hold onto this feeling for a long time. Because if the CFP expands to 24 teams next year, it may be the last time something as dramatic ever happens in September.

Part of what makes college football so intoxicating is the knowledge that, eventually, the cloud of smoke will lift and we'll see everything clearly. To experience that before we even play the games won't be nearly as fun.

articles.title: Manchester derby: Fixed v fluid - opposite approaches Maresca and Carrick are taking
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca and Michael Carrick will go head to head in Sunday's Manchester derby, with their teams set up very differently.
articles.body:
There are many things that Manchester City and Manchester United have in common - but one thing decisively separates them this season.

Based just five miles apart and united by a shared desire to return to the top of the Premier League, their gameplans are almost diametrically opposed.

The best teams in the world often play in similar ways, as demonstrated in last season's Champions League final between between Paris St-Germain and Arsenal - teams who use similar shapes, look to dominate the ball, and encourage rotations into fixed positions.

But looking ahead to Sunday's Manchester derby, expect to see City boss Enzo Maresca and his United counterpart Michael Carrick field teams teams that play in a totally different way to each other.

In short, City use a rigid structure with players precisely positioned, while United have a more fluid approach that has some positional guidelines but allows players the freedom to roam - here is how it works in detail.

Teams need to adapt to fixture scheduling - Maresca

Two goals in two games - Sesko gives Man Utd a different threat

Striking a balance between control and freedom

Maresca, inspired by mentor and former City boss Pep Guardiola, hopes to create a side synonymous with control, dominating as much of the ball as possible, looking to reduce the uncertainty that comes with playing football.

The Italian has often compared the move-based nature of chess to football, so it is not a surprise that positional play is the foundation of his sides.

These are ideas that have proved successful in modern football but Carrick's United deviate from this approach more than most.

This is not to say there are not positional ideas in Carrick's United.

There are, as we will go on to highlight, but they are certainly a smaller part of his game when compared to Maresca.

This balance is illustrated well in Carrick's quotes about how he first managed 21-year-old midfielder Kobbie Mainoo.

"I [was] really conscious of not giving him an awful lot [of instructions]," he said. "A couple of little pointers, a few positional things, but to trust in what he is. He's a fantastic footballer."

How Carrick's United use positional ideas

United keep their two centre-backs in fixed positions.

In United's midfield the deepest midfielder is tasked with helping in build-up play, either as part of a narrow midfield two - alongside United's second midfielder - or by dropping deep to create a back three with the centre-backs.

If the back three is created, the second midfielder holds his position in the centre of midfield alone.

The full-backs begin by holding more natural left and right full-back positions in build-up play. Higher up the pitch, they may join the attacking line.

When this happens, they position themselves based on their team-mate on the wing - with one out wide and one more central.

Meanwhile, the number 10 and striker have looked to drop deep, forming what looks more like a fluid front two at times.

With the holding midfielder given the license to drop to form a temporary back three, United have the option to overload teams that press with two strikers.

Against narrow teams, United's wide full-backs give them an option to play around the opposition, but Carrick's men often look to play through the middle of the pitch instead - something that appears they have been coached to do.

The positions of the full-backs help by enticing narrow opponents to be stretched wider. Concerned by the threat of United's full-backs in space, the opposition may move over, which frees up space for team-mates to pass the ball into the midfielders in the centre of the pitch.

By playing into the middle even when it is congested, United draw opponents towards the ball. This results in Carrick's wide men finding themselves with more time and space on the ball.

The central clusters of players set United up to try and crowd around the ball if it is lost, hoping to win it back.

How Carrick and Maresca view player freedom

The shapes and positions outlined above give United's players a framework to start from.

But players who able to impact the game from different parts of the pitch are trusted to move more freely. This gives United a level of unpredictability which comes with pros and cons.

If Fernandes or Cunha decide that the game requires them to move close to the ball, away from the middle and closer to the touchline, they will do so.

Central defenders then face a difficult decision over whether or not to follow them.

If they are not picked up, United often find themselves outnumbering the opposition around the ball, which makes it easier for them to escape pressure.

If they are marked, space opens up in the middle of the opposition defence for another player to exploit.

Then it is up to the United players to interpret a more chaotic picture of the game, with players free to decide what to do next in that moment rather than follow a set script.

"If the freedom for you is that you can move everywhere, that is not freedom, that is chaos," he told Sky Sports last September.

"[Our] freedom? You can do what you want in the position you receive the ball."

Manchester City 's starting XI occupy specific zones on the pitch in their 3-2-5 or 3-1-3-3 shape on the ball.

This makes their approach more predictable for opponents but it means that City's players know each player's role, where they are likely to be positioned and how they are likely to move.

After City's win against Coventry, Maresca said that Iliman Ndiaye had had minimal training time and explained that meant sometimes "he was moving in the wrong way [into the] wrong position" for how City intend to play.

The advantage of this more fixed style is that, even if opponents know what is coming, the speed of execution can still make it difficult to stop.

Also, less spontaneous thinking is required to unlock a defence as solutions are set out by their manager and drilled through repetition over a season.

How Carrick introduces order within his more free system

To give this freer approach some direction, United appear to have established a set of shared tactical principles and concepts.

This includes clustering around the ball, attracting pressure, before looking to find players in space quickly.

Unlike Maresca's more specific solutions, which outline where and when certain actions should be taken, it is often United's players who decide when and where to use what they've been taught.

Watching how United pass the ball illustrates this point well.

Carrick's United look to escape pressure through trios of players passing the ball between each other. As one player is about to receive the ball, a team-mate will often move to become the next passing option.

They do not do this in fixed zones but look to create these triangles when they feel like the moment is right.

This shared tactical language gives them a level of clarity whilst being unpredictable for the defending side.

There is no right or wrong way to play football but, as this piece has attempted to showcase, every approach has its positives and negatives.

United's freer approach has been praised by the maverick Fernandes, who saw a boost in his output following Carrick's appointment last season and was subsequently crowned Premier League Player of the Season.

Conversely, there have been questions raised around City's use of the creative Rayan Cherki.

On numerous occasions last season, Guardiola made clear he felt the Frenchman would be more effective staying between the lines, close to Erling Haaland.

"He has the ability and quality in the final third. That's why I sometimes say when they go to the goalkeeper for the ball I say no, I want you there in the final third."

Maresca has echoed this sentiment, perhaps not as strongly, explaining: "There is always a gameplan. When we are in our [half], Rayan drops a little bit to manage the tempo [of] the game [but] when the ball is in the opposite [half] we need Rayan in a position to be dangerous."

Some may argue that Fernandes has been maximised individually by United in a way that Cherki has not yet been by City - but the other side of the argument would be to say that City look better than United as a whole at this early part of the season.

Creating a freer style of play requires a chemistry and understanding between players that takes time to develop, while fixed roles and patterns of play can be implemented sooner and provide consistency irrespective of which players start.

Whether Carrick's bet will pay off is yet to be seen but in a world dominated by coaches successfully prescribing solutions, giving some control back to the players is a welcome alternative - at least for the neutral.

articles.title: Sergio Camello, el 'rockero' del gol: "Tiene todo el talento y el arte"
articles.standfirst: El atacante madrileño anotó gol frente al Real Madrid y sigue en lo alto por el Pichichi
articles.summary: El atacante madrileño anotó gol frente al Real Madrid y sigue en lo alto por el Pichichi
articles.body: El partido del Rayo Vallecano en el Bernabéu tuvo luces y sombras. Los dos primeros goles con errores impropios de Lejeune afearon la primera parte de un Rayo Vallecano que se fue 3-0 por debajo al descanso. Sin embargo, en la segunda parte, el equipo de Beñat San José salió como si de un 0-0 se tratara y 'mordió' en el Bernabéu. En el minuto 46 llegó un disparo de Pedro Díaz al palo de Courtois y en el minuto 51 ocurrió lo que lleva ocurriendo en los últimos cuatro partidos del cuadro franjirrojo. El gol de Camello. El delantero madrileño aprovechó una pérdida del Real Madrid en campo propio a causa de la presión rayista para empujar el balón a la red y sumar así su sexto gol de la temporada. El atacante suma seis dianas en los cinco primeros encuentros del Rayo Vallecano y es el Pichichi junto a Raphinha y a Mbappé. Camello está a tan solo dos dianas de igualar su mejor prestación goleadora que tuvo lugar la pasada campaña. Los dos últimos tantos que marcó la temporada anterior fueron en los dos últimos partidos, por lo que se podría decir que lleva una racha de ocho goles en sus últimos seis encuentros de la liga doméstica. En estos momentos, es el quinto máximo goleador del Rayo en Primera división con 23 goles, superando los 22 de Bolic. Sergio Camello, ídolo de la afición tanto dentro como fuera del campo, salió del césped del Bernabéu algo molesto, pero Beñat San José en rueda de prensa le quitó hierro al asunto. "Se ha quejado de unas molestias y de que ha tardado el cambio. Le he dicho que estuviera tranquilo y luego como es un tipo espectacular, me ha dicho 'nada míster estaba un poco caliente', pero nada más", afirmó el técnico vasco antes de elogiarle. "Tiene todo el talento y el arte, es el jugador tan completo que es y sobre todo que trabaja un montón. Lo que más me gusta de él es como trabaja él y todo el equipo. Estoy muy contento con todo el equipo y en el día a día con los jugadores", finalizó el técnico vasco. Cinéfilo, rockero y campeón olímpico, Sergio Camello sigue alzando la voz cada vez que juega el Rayo Vallecano y su equipo lo agradece. Sea en Vallecas, en Butarque o en el Bernabéu, este delantero se deja la piel por su escudo.

articles.title: Robert Moreno llega a Corea del Sur: "El objetivo es que la afición se sienta orgullosa"
articles.standfirst: El técnico español dirigirá los próximos seis partidos a la selección asiática, hasta el 27 de noviembre, y después la federación evaluará y decidirá
articles.summary: El técnico español dirigirá los próximos seis partidos a la selección asiática, hasta el 27 de noviembre, y después la federación evaluará y decidirá
articles.body: Robert Moreno, nuevo técnico interino de la selección masculina de fútbol de Corea del Sur, llegó este domingo al país asiático, donde prometió unir a los jugadores para que los aficionados se enorgullezcan del equipo. "Vamos a trabajar al máximo para (...) unir a todos, generar un equipo y hacer que la afición se sienta orgullosa. Es el objetivo", dijo el técnico de L'Hospitalet de Llobregat (Barcelona, 1977) en declaraciones a medios a su llegada al aeropuerto de Incheon, ciudad situada al oeste de Seúl. En su primer mensaje a los seguidores de los 'Guerreros Taeguk', Moreno, quien cumplirá 49 años el 19 de septiembre, manifestó que llega al país con "mucha ilusión, mucha responsabilidad por el puesto, y orgulloso" de dirigir a esta selección. "Es una de las mejores de Asia", subrayó. En cuanto al resultado de Corea del Sur en la Copa del Mundo disputada en Estados Unidos, México y Canadá, en la que quedó eliminada en la fase de grupos, dijo que entendía que es un "momento que no le gusta a nadie", pero que iba a analizar "con tranquilidad" lo ocurrido. No obstante, el técnico, que fue asistente de Luis Enrique durante su paso por la selección española, consideró que ahora tienen que centrarse en el nuevo trabajo, "mirar hacia delante", sin olvidarse de lo que ha pasado. Moreno dirigió nueve partidos al equipo nacional en 2019, primero durante la ausencia de Luis Enrique y, posteriormente, tras su salida del cargo, en ambos casos por motivos personales. Tras su paso por el combinado nacional, dirigió al Mónaco, al Granada y, por último, al Sochi, en el que estuvo al frente hasta septiembre de 2025. La Asociación de Fútbol de Corea del Sur (KFA) aprobó a principios de mes su nombramiento como técnico del combinado nacional masculino, con un contrato vigente hasta el 27 de noviembre, por lo que abarcará seis encuentros internacionales. Así, debutará el 24 de septiembre ante Ecuador en Corea del Sur y cuatro días después se enfrentará a Uruguay, mientras que en octubre el combinado surcoreano jugará contra Venezuela, el día 2, y Uzbekistán, el 6. Tras este periodo, la federación surcoreana evaluará su trabajo con la opción de ampliar su etapa hasta la Copa Asiática de Arabia Saudí a principios de 2027. La federación surcoreana destacó su capacidad para utilizar datos en el diseño táctico y el análisis de los rivales, así como su conocimiento del fútbol del país asiático y las alternativas tácticas planteadas durante el proceso de selección. Su contratación supone además la primera vez que la KFA elige al seleccionador masculino mediante una convocatoria pública. Moreno cubre el puesto que permanecía vacante desde el Mundial, después de que Hong Myung-bo dimitiera tras la eliminación de la selección, nombramiento que estuvo rodeado de polémica por falta de transparencia e irregularidades en el proceso.

articles.title: Fantasy football start or sit Week 1: Kyler Murray, Jaxson Dart, Jordan Love
articles.summary: Week 1 fantasy football start or sit advice for Kyler Murray, Jordan Love and Jaxson Dart.
articles.body:
With Week 1 here, we're doling out some fantasy football start or sit advice for New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart , Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love .

Murray is getting a fresh start in Minnesota after his time in Arizona ended this offseason, and both Dart and Love are hoping to take another step forward in their careers after up-and-down campaigns for both in 2025.

Are any of these three signal-callers worthy of a spot in your starting lineup in Week 1?

Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) warms up before a game against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium. Credit: John Jones-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

With no Micah Parsons (PUP list) or Rashan Gary (traded), the Packers' pass-rush is weaker than it was last season, and there is nothing scary about Green Bay 's cornerbacks room.

Murray offers a safe floor thanks to his rushing ability, and he's playing for a head coach in Kevin O'Connell who has a history of reviving the career of a down-and-out quarterback.

Adding to that, this might be the best supporting cast Murray has ever had with guys like Justin Jefferson , Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings at wide receiver.

Consider me a believer in Murray with the Vikings. He's in our lineup in Week 1.

New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart (6) high fives his teammates during a preseason opening game between the New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings on Saturday, Aug. 15, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

There's a lot of hype surrounding the Cowboys' defense after an offseason overhaul, but we have to see it to believe it after Dallas sported a putrid defense last season.

Even if the Cowboys' defense is better, there's a scenario in which the Giants are chasing points and forced to throw a ton if their defense has issues slowing down Dallas' offense.

I expect Malik Nabers to play, which will help Dart's cause, and his rushing ability gives him another avenue to pick up points.

Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) passes against the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first quarter at Acrisure Stadium. Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Love was not an effective fantasy quarterback last season, ranking as QB21 overall in fantasy points per game, per Fantasy Pros .

And he doesn't draw a favorable matchup in Week 1 against a Vikings defense that gave up the second-fewest passing yards per game last season.

Minnesota traded Jonathan Greenard , but the team still has two good edge rushers, and Brian Flores knows how to create pressure in other ways.

This has all the makings of a rough game for Love, and I don't feel comfortable starting him this week.

articles.title: “Overrated”: Skip Bayless Goes All Out Against Oklahoma OC as Sooners Face ‘Season-Killing Loss’ vs Michigan
articles.summary: The Oklahoma Sooners massively hurt their College Football Playoff qualification chances by losing 17-10 to the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Ann Arbor....
articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners massively hurt their College Football Playoff qualification chances by losing 17-10 to the Michigan Wolverines on Saturday in Ann Arbor. After a massive 51-0 win over UTEP in the season opener, the loss surprised many.

After the loss, sports commentator Skip Bayless unleashed fury on Oklahoma's offense, particularly targeting their offensive coordinator Ben Arbuckle and quarterback John Mateer . The Sooners quarterback completed 17-of-33 passes for 189 yards, one TD and one interception, while adding 45 rushing yards. Bayless compared Mateer's performance with Michigan quarterback Bryce Underwood . The commentator also said this loss will sting Oklahoma in the end.

"Last year John Mateer outplayed Bryce Underwood at OU," Bayless wrote. "This year, just the opposite at Michigan. Mateer just too inaccurate, indecisive. Receivers didn't help him. Neither did run game or O line. D hung in but without Kip Lewis , overrated. Season-killing loss."

Bayless noted all sorts of errors in Oklahoma's offense, ranging from receivers and the running game to problems in the offensive line.

Mateer could only pass for 52 yards while running back Lloyd Avant was handed the ball just five times in the first half. The offensive line also allowed multiple pass rush moments, including one sack against Mateer. As a result, the Sooners quarterback not only had a bad day on the passing front but also faced rushing pressure from Michigan.

Underwood was a major difference-maker for Michigan. The Wolverines' quarterback rushed for 87 yards, including an explosive 38-yard rushing touchdown in the first quarter. He also passed for 111 yards.

Oklahoma QB John Mateer's Interception Proved Vital For Michigan

Oklahoma was shut out in the first half and trailed 10-0 at halftime. Michigan scored a touchdown in the first quarter and a field goal in the second quarter.

The Sooners finally got on board in the third quarter when John Mateer connected with Mackenzie Alleyne for a 22-yard touchdown. In the early fourth quarter, the Sooners tied the game 10-10 with the help of Tate Sandell 's 34-yard field goal.

However, the turning point came with 7:53 remaining in the game. Michigan's Jyaire Hill intercepted Mateer and quickly converted the turnover into Jordan Marshall 's go-ahead 1-yard TD.

The loss was significant because Michigan was unranked while Oklahoma was No. 11. The Wolverines avenged their 24-13 loss from last season.

articles.title: Serie A Preview: Napoli vs Bologna – Team News, Lineups & Prediction
articles.summary: Napoli will look to shake off frustration after a disappointing Champions League opener when they take on Bologna at home today. With both managers under hea...
articles.body:
Napoli will look to shake off frustration after a disappointing Champions League opener when they take on Bologna at home today. With both managers under heavy scrutiny, this meeting between the two early-season strugglers could determine the fate of Massimiliano Allegri and Domenico Tedesco.

Wednesday's 1-0 home defeat to Arsenal marked Napoli's third consecutive loss in all competitions. As the pressure builds on Allegri, last season's Serie A runners-up return to the Diego Maradona Stadium seeking a much-needed win amid the club's worst three-game start to a new top-flight campaign since 2015/16.

Allegri's overly cautious approach cost Napoli dearly last week as they squandered a two-goal lead in a heartbreaking 3-2 defeat at Inter. It's fair to admit they were a bit unfortunate, considering Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa wasted a glorious chance to re-establish their advantage a moment before Lautaro Martinez 's winner.

Like Allegri, Tedesco is already under fire just three league matches into his tenure at Renato Dall'Ara. After a pair of narrow 1-0 losses to Atalanta and Lazio , Bologna scored a last-minute equalizer to hold Sassuolo to a dramatic 2-2 home draw last weekend, avoiding the ignominy of starting a new top-flight season with three successive defeats for the first time in the club's history.

However, that doesn't change the fact that they last had fewer points at this stage of a campaign 11 years ago. Therefore, Tedesco may already be fighting for his life in Emilia-Romagna, and Napoli could put the final nail in his coffin as Bologna manager.

Despite a 2-0 win at Genoa on the opening Serie A weekend, Allegri has done little to silence his detractors at the start of his career in Naples. Furthermore, Napoli have reportedly lined up Raffaele Palladino as his potential successor as the Partenopei stare down the barrel of a third consecutive home defeat for the first time since November 2020.

Achieving that unwanted feat would see Napoli lose three league matches on the trot for the first time since January 2020. Needless to say, it might be detrimental to Allegri's tenure at the Maradona Stadium, but the former Milan and Juventus manager can draw confidence from his stellar managerial record against Bologna here.

Indeed, Allegri has faced the Rossoblu 26 times without ever losing as a manager (W19, D7), suggesting Napoli could be well-positioned to end a two-game losing streak in this fixture. Adding to this sentiment, the four-time Italian champions had only lost once in their 11 encounters against Bologna prior to this run (W6, D4).

Tedesco could salvage his disastrous Serie A start by helping Bologna equal a long-awaited historic feat here. The Rossoblu last won three consecutive clashes against Napoli in the 1930s, but their recent results at the Maradona Stadium fail to inspire much confidence, as they've lost nine of their last 12 visits here (W3).

Bologna suffered a morale-crushing defeat at Atalanta in their first away game of the season, but their road form since February has been stellar. Only Como (7) have won more Serie A away games than Bologna's six in that period, and that record carries more weight when considered that those victories came from only eight matches (L2).

However, a lack of firepower could pose a genuine threat to Bologna's quest to post their first league win under Tedesco. In addition to drawing a blank in their opening two Serie A outings, the visitors have failed to score in nine of their last 13 away league losses.

Napoli suffered a double injury blow against Arsenal, with Alisson Santos and Alex Meret both forced off with fitness problems. Therefore, Vanja Milinkovic-Savic is likely to start in goal, while David Neres could take his countryman's place in attack. Scott McTominay , Giovane, Alessandro Buongiorno , and Luca Marianucci are the remaining notable absentees in the home squad.

As for Bologna, Artem Dovbyk has joined Riccardo Orsolini and Oussama El Azzouzi on the sidelines. That's concerning, given that the Ukrainian striker scored a late equalizer against Sassuolo, leaving misfiring Roberto Piccoli as the only out-and-out striker at Tedesco's disposal for this pivotal showdown.

Napoli vs Bologna Potential Starting Lineups

Napoli (4-3-3): Milinkovic-Savic; Di Lorenzo , Rrahmani , Marin, Spinazzola ; Gilmour, Lobotka , De Bruyne ; Politano , Hojlund, Neres.

Bologna (4-2-3-1): Skorupski ; Holm, Heggem, Theate , Miranda; Ferguson, Moro; Bernardeschi , Odgaard , Cambiaghi ; Piccoli.

Allegri can ill afford a failure in this fixture if he's to weather the storm, and Bologna's underwhelming start to the season paints a promising picture for the Italian manager. We don't expect the visitors to go down without a fight, but Napoli should take care of business here.

articles.title: 🤩 I score however I want: best Bundesliga comeback ever?
articles.summary: There were quite a few doubters about striker Niclas Füllkrug’s return to SV Werder Bremen. He seems to have made it his mission to prove the critics wrong....
articles.body:
There were quite a few doubters about striker Niclas Füllkrug's return to SV Werder Bremen . He seems to have made it his mission to prove the critics wrong. And it really does seem to be a perfect match between the club from the Weser and the 24-time Germany international .

Yesterday, he rescued a point for his new old club at 1. FC Köln. In the 69th minute, Füllkrug scored the 1-1 equalizer, much to the delight of his own fans, and in doing so also sealed the final score. He then celebrated his goal extensively in front of the traveling green-and-white supporters.

After the final whistle, he once again made it clear at the 'Sky' microphone just how happy he is with how things have gone since his return to the Bundesliga and to Werder after three years away: "After my goal, I ran over to the stands and shouted: 'How does that work?' How is it that I put this shirt on and start scoring again however I want? Beautiful story," said the striker.

His coach is raving about Füllkrug too, as you can see here in the video.

It was not his first competitive goal since joining on loan from West Ham United in the summer. He had already found the net in typical Füllkrug fashion in last week's 3-1 win over RB Leipzig .

For all Werder fans—and for the number nine himself—one can only hope that he stays fit and that things continue just like this.

And who knows, maybe he will soon play his way back onto the call-up list of Germany coach Jürgen Klopp in the Bundesliga.

What do you think? Is a "Fülle" in top form still good enough for the national team? Write it in the comments!

articles.title: Ryan Day faced a choice for Ohio State. He made a terrible call | Opinion
articles.summary: Of all the jobs on a bloated college football staff, is there no “odds coach” who could’ve talked sense into Ryan Day?
articles.body:
Of all the jobs on a bloated college football staff, is there no "odds coach" who could've talked sense into Ryan Day ?

I don't have the percentages in front of me — an "odds coach" could help with that — but I know this: I'd rather be trailing by one point, with possession of the ball, a minute to play, and a timeout in my pocket, than down by a point, with possession, 25 seconds and no timeouts.

The former is what would've happened if Day had opted to let Texas score, uncontested, on 1st-and-goal from the Ohio State 1-yard line. Instead, Day thought his Buckeyes could stuff Texas four times in a row.

They got two stops, and Day burned his last timeout in the process. When Texas punched it in on third down, Ohio State had no timeouts and just 25 seconds to get into field-goal range.

"We talked about it, and decided that we were gonna play defense on second down (instead of letting Texas score)," Day told reporters after Ohio State's fourth-quarter collapse in a 24-23 loss to Texas.

Second down? Buddy, you should've let 'em score on first down.

Kirk Herbstreit mentioned that option on 1st-and-goal. Too bad the ABC broadcast feed wasn't pumping into Day's headphones.

Texas Longhorns and Ohio State Buckeyes meet in Austin

Ryan Day has a loss to rival 2022 Sugar Bowl

True, if Ohio State had stopped Texas four times in a row from the 1, we'd be talking about Day's gutsiness and his belief in his defense.

Never mind guts, though. This is math, and it's just tough to argue.

Your chances are better trailing 24-23 with 60 seconds to go, plus a timeout, as compared to 24-23, no timeouts and 25 seconds left.

Seems obvious, right? Or, at least it would be to an "odds coach." Just not to a highly paid college football coach.

Remember this as the biggest choke-job of Day's career.

He finally endured a collapse even worse than Ohio State blowing a 14-point fourth-quarter lead in the 2022 Sugar Bowl. Three years prior to that, Day's Buckeyes blew a 16-point lead against Clemson in playoff semifinal.

Now, here's a collapse to trump them all, even if the result isn't as damaging.

When Georgia rallied past Ohio State in that 2022 Sugar Bowl, it meant Day had to wait two more years to win a national championship.

Thanks to a playoff big enough to accommodate two- and maybe even a three-loss teams, this result isn't as damaging, but it's more appalling.

Ryan Day after Ohio State blows it: 'This one hurts.'

How's this for some math? ESPN gave Ohio State a win probability of more than 98% when it led by 20 points ahead of the fourth quarter.

"We have to win the fourth quarter," Day said, "… and we didn't do that."

Arch Manning and Texas stole it. Day and the Buckeyes blew it .

Manning's Heisman odds improved, especially when you pair this result with Dante Moore and Oregon withering in a stunning loss to Oklahoma State. The Texas quarterback raced around the field afterward with a look of unbridled joy on his face, as if he understood he'd supplied a signature victory and a comeback that could start to alter his legacy — and that of his coach, Steve Sarkisian .

If you think Day handled the end-of-game situation correctly, you're probably pointing out the Buckeyes only mustered three points after halftime, and their second-half offensive sputter included two three-and-outs. You'd point out Connor Hawkins already missed a field goal from 45 yards in the fourth quarter that could've sealed the victory.

Even so, I'd take my chances with 60 seconds of game time, a timeout, and the best wide receiver in college football on the field. Granted, if Jeremiah Smith would've secured Julian Sayin's deep shot on third down, ahead of Hawkins' missed field goal, the Buckeyes wouldn't have needed any last-minute heroics. Smith looked sensational for 2½ quarters, but he didn't have another reception in the final 24 minutes.

As Ohio State's lead dwindled, it forced Day to make a stressful decision. He made the wrong call. What are the odds?

Blake Toppmeyer is the USA TODAY Network's senior national college football columnist. Listen to his podcast, " College Football Unfiltered ." Email him at BToppmeyer@gannett.com and follow him on X @btoppmeyer .

articles.title: Hawkeye Football: The Morning After Iowa State vs Iowa
articles.summary: Iowa’s passing game helps the Hawks cement the victory as they escape with a 16-13 win over ISU
articles.body:
The Cyclones came to Kinnick hoping to spoil Iowa 's massive recruiting weekend, but in a traditional Cy-Hawk fashion, Iowa survived on a game winning field goal and got to hoist the trophy to take it back home to its rightful resting place.

I was fuming at the end of this game and didn't feel a whole lot better when I woke up this morning. It's only Week 2, and yet somehow ISU has cobbled together a group of portal transfers to take this one down to the wire. Are they really that good, or is Iowa possibly bad? With that thought in mind, I am going to go with The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly. Only in reverse order.

Iowa looked unimaginative on offense and first down in particular. On week 1 we saw multiple passes on first down and creativity in the offense like there hasn't been in years. It felt like Iowa regressed in this game.

On punt returns, Reece Vander Zee either called fair catches or let the ball roll. Indeed, it wasn't until the fourth quarter that Reece actually returned a punt (and there were a lot of punts!). We didn't see Evan James field a punt return until late in the game. This is better than punting is winning, because not attempting to return punts is even better!

Iowa attempted multiple quarterback sneaks. They did not work. Someone needs to tell the coaching staff that Mark Gronwski graduated last year.

Iowa had a number of issues in the red zone for week 1. Week 2, we don't know if it has been solved, because they hardly ever got there.

Iowa rushing averaged 3.2 yards per carry and had 93 yards total rushing. It sure didn't feel good. Perhaps ISU's group of portal transfers is really that good in Week 2, but I have serious doubts.

ISU quarterback Jaylen Raynor wasn't pressured that much and was never sacked, against an ISU offensive line that wasn't know for being a strength of their team.

Cam Buffington had 10 tackles at halftime, and 15 total tackles to end the game, and this was just his second start ever (in Week 2). Jayden Montgomery and Jaylen Watson performed quite well, as did the linebackers in general. During fall camp the coaching staff said they felt this group was deep with seven or eight guys who they expected would contribute.

Other than quarterback sneaks, Brown did a decent job of rushing the football and scored a touchdown in the second quarter on an end around to the left. He also stayed calm when under pressure and delivered multiple strikes as the pocket began to collapse.

Okay, this isn't Iowa football , but after OSU was leading #4 Texas 23 – 3 in the third quarter, they ended up losing 23 – 24. I hate OSU, and while I was fuming after the Iowa game, this news made me sleep better last night.

Unlike Iowa's offense, I decided to change it up and add an element of surprise, so let's talk about the real hero of this game! Caden Buhr, a walk-on who got his first ever start in Week 1, nailed all three field goals perfectly through the middle, scored 10 of Iowa's 16 points, and kicked the game winning field goal with 19 seconds remaining. Give that man a scholarship!
